title: Safety-Critical Traffic Simulation with Adversarial Transfer of Driving Intentions

control_signal.value: Adversarial driving intention, i.e. the actor's final goal position, found automatically by constrained optimisation to collide with the AV; not user-specified.

control_mechanism.value: Decoupled two stages: optimisation finds the adversarial goal, then a goal-conditioned motion prediction model fills in realistic intermediate trajectory toward that goal, with dynamic replanning.

base_model.value: Goal-based trajectory prediction model with MTR-style encoder-decoder (MLP polyline encoders, multi-head attention) trained on real-world data; AV treated as a black box, estimated by sampling trajectories as in CAT.

datasets.value: nuScenes and Waymo (Waymo run in MetaDrive); planners are log replay, rule-based (STRIVE) and RL-based TD3 (CAT).

metrics.value: AV collision rate, opponent off-road and global off-road rate, in-road and collision rate, Wasserstein acceleration/jerk distance, generation time; closed-loop AV collision, off-road, route completion.

controllability_evidence.value: Ablation on nuScenes: without intention transfer collision is 1.4; with optimised transfer 40.6 at 10.4 global off-road; random-interpolation goal gives 75.9 collision but 24.1 global off-road. Waymo RL planner: 45.3 vs CAT 36.7.

stated_limitations.value: Focuses on collisions between two agents; more complex multi-agent accidents are only limitedly considered.

notes: An attack/adversarial simulator, not user-steerable generation; the control signal is solved by the optimiser. Collision numbers in ablation are from Table IV (units presumably percent, not stated in snippet).
